response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), s AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg FROM g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, avg_net_fee_rate - side_avg AS diff_from_side_avg FROM s WHERE avg_net_fee_rate > side_avg ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The record count is the number of fee records in each group (COUNT(*)) after the feerate filter and the join to orders, including records whose rebrate is null. Those records add to the count but not to the average, because a null rebrate makes the net rate null.
orders.recordvault is unique per order, so the join does not duplicate fee records.
The side average is the unweighted mean of the group averages for that side. Groups whose average is null are left out of it.
